messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] latency.p99 % increase detected (service: inference-api, region: us-west-2). Threshold 700ms breached. Current p99=1.35s. Paging oncall-sre :rotating_light:

oncall-sre: acked. I'm looking. pinging Maya and Praveen for visibility.

Maya: on it. pulling p95/p99 by route now.

Praveen: I see streaming stalls on the realtime route in the dashboard — active connections spiking and several stalled sessions. link: https://dash.redwood/inference/latency?range=15m

oncall-sre: quick checks:
- are infra autoscalers healthy?
- any recent deploys to inference runtime?
- are we hitting kernel OOMs on nodes?

svc-ops: autoscaler shows normal scale events but a few pods in restarting state (3/60). kube events show OOMKilled on gpu-pool-5-7.

Maya: pulling recent deploys: no infra deploys in last 2 hours. There was a model variant rollout 12m ago for v2-clarity -> slightly larger memory footprint.

Praveen: running live query on p99 by model:
```
SELECT model, percentile(latency_ms, 99) FROM requests WHERE region='us-west-2' GROUP BY model
```
Results: v2-clarity p99=1.8s, baseline-1 p99=520ms. Most of the tail is on v2-clarity.

oncall-sre: hypothesis: rollout of v2-clarity increased KV cache churn + memory pressure leading to streaming stalls and tail latency. Immediate mitigation: route traffic off v2-clarity in us-west-2 if safe.

Alice: tagging in ops-runbook for model rollbacks. If we can switch routing policy to fallback_model for canary traffic (20% -> 0) that should reduce load on v2-clarity.

svc-ops: starting routing change now. Command: `rwctl route set --service inference-api --region us-west-2 --model-policy fallback_model --selector model=v2-clarity --percent=0`

oncall-sre: confirmed command executed, saw traffic shift logs: 95% of canary requests moved to baseline-1 within 30s.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] routing change detected by telemetry. p95 dropped from 420ms to 210ms within 90s. p99 improving but still elevated at ~720ms.

Maya: looking into node OOMs. kube node metrics show memory climb correlated with v2-clarity session ramp. One node shows repeated restarts (gpu-pool-5-7). Starting a pod eviction to drain unhealthy nodes.

Praveen: overlaying KV cache hit-rate: hit-rate fell from 88% -> 54% for v2-clarity prefix caches during the spike. That corroborates cache churn causing increased compute per request.

oncall-sre: mitigation summary so far: 1) traffic routed off v2-clarity 2) unhealthy node drained 3) autoscaler holding. Customer impact: estimated 3% of total production requests saw >1s latency during window. No complete request failures reported. Notifying support to prepare customer comms for any affected SLAs.

Alice: opening a postmortem ticket and tagging product owners. Also will start a rollback of the v2-clarity rollout in the model registry if we confirm memory regression.

svc-ops: node drain completed, replaced node back to pool healthy, no new OOMs after routing change.

EngLeadBot: can we capture a flamegraph or pprof of one of the restarted pods for offline analysis? add to ticket RW-2981.

Maya: yes capturing heap dump + KV cache metrics. Uploading to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/1872/clarity-heap-1869004321.tgz

Praveen: next actions:
- full rollback of v2-clarity in us-west-2 (if e2e checks pass)
- run a synthetic load to validate cache restoration
- add guardrails to model rollout to detect memory + cache anomalies earlier

oncall-sre: scheduling handoff: I'm going to escalate to SRE on-call lead and handoff to night oncall in 30m. Current state: latency stabilized p95=220ms p99=560ms after routing change; monitoring until next hour.

Maya: adding notes to incident channel and setting severity to Sev2.

Praveen: support ticket updated with impact numbers and affected customers (internal list).

oncall-sre: handing off to svc-ops for monitoring. If p99 creeps over 800ms or node restarts >1 in 15m, page oncall-sre again. Leaving open. :white_check_mark:
